rationale: FEAT-397 already defines and ships the per-round usage contract for five clients; this is a known, well-scoped extension of an existing pattern to two AWS clients that were an explicit non-goal. Research must pin down the exact contract, the reference implementation to copy, and the Bedrock/Nova call sites that need it.

queries.intent: Read the FEAT-397 spec to extract the exact per-round observability contract that Bedrock/Nova must satisfy
Read AbstractClient._emit_round_event and ClientRoundEvent to learn the primitives Bedrock/Nova must reuse
Read AIMessage.usage / total_usage() and CompletionUsage to learn the accumulation target and extra_usage['rounds'] convention
Read BedrockClient / BedrockConverseBase ask() and its tool loop to locate exactly where per-round usage must be accumulated and emitted
Read NovaClient to determine whether it inherits BedrockConverseBase's tool loop or drives its own
Find the reference FEAT-397 implementation in an already-migrated client (Anthropic) to copy the accumulation + emission pattern verbatim
Locate how Bedrock/Nova currently parse Converse API usage (inputTokens/outputTokens/totalTokens) so accumulation reuses existing extraction
Read the reference client's ask() tool loop end-to-end as the implementation template
Find FEAT-397 tests to learn the test contract new Bedrock/Nova tests must mirror
Identify downstream consumers of ClientRoundEvent (recorders, metrics subscribers) to confirm no consumer-side change is needed
Check the Nova audio/streaming path for a separate usage surface that per-round observability would also need to cover
Review recent commit activity on bedrock.py and nova/ to detect in-flight work that could conflict
Locate the three other FEAT-397 holdout clients (ClaudeAgentClient, TransformersClient, GeminiLiveClient) to assess whether they belong in this feature's scope
queries.note: Added at the Phase-1 gate on user request (widened scope).

queries.intent: Inspect ClaudeAgentClient and TransformersClient tool loops to judge whether the FEAT-397 pattern applies unchanged or needs a different treatment
queries.note: Added at the Phase-1 gate on user request (widened scope).

expected_findings: The precise FEAT-397 per-round contract: accumulate CompletionUsage across rounds, emit ClientRoundEvent per round, set accumulated total on AIMessage.usage, record round count in usage.extra_usage['rounds'].
Whether BedrockClient and NovaClient share one tool loop (BedrockConverseBase) so a single change covers both, or need two separate changes.
The exact insertion points in the Bedrock/Nova tool loops.
Whether ClaudeAgentClient / TransformersClient / GeminiLiveClient should be in or out of scope.
Whether the Nova streaming/voice path has a usage surface FEAT-397 does not model.
